blocks.text: Why PDF data extraction is a major financial analysis problem

PDFs are inherently static. They treat data as a collection of shapes and text blocks rather than structured cells. When you receive a bank statement or an invoice as a PDF, your computer does not see a table. It sees a flat image or a sequence of text strings. This forces you to copy and paste, which is where the trouble begins.
The hidden costs of manual extraction

The cost of this problem is not just your time. It is the operational risk that comes with every manual keystroke. When you manually move data, you introduce a 1% error rate on average. In a large model, one wrong sign or a missed decimal point can ruin your entire forecast. Beyond the errors, there is the burnout factor. Over half of finance professionals report that repetitive data tasks contribute to high turnover risk.
Why these documents are so hard to parse

items: Inconsistent layouts across different financial institutions.
Scanned images that require high-quality OCR to be readable.
Tables that span across multiple pages, breaking the data flow.
Ambiguous date formats or currency symbols that confuse automated tools.
Password protection which blocks standard import tools entirely.

blocks.text: Fixes anyone can use on a Mac

You do not need an enterprise budget to stop the copy-paste cycle. Start by looking at your source. If you can get an API feed or a CSV download from your bank, do that first. If you must use a PDF, use specialized local tools. Tabula is a free, open-source tool that handles simple table extraction well on macOS. For more complex needs, consider privacy-focused tools that process data on your own machine.
Always check your employer's policy on data privacy before uploading sensitive financial documents to any online tool. If you handle client or patient data, use only approved, secure software.

blocks.text: Lazur helps you speed up the cleanup process. When you have a PDF open on one side of your screen and Excel on the other, hold ⌥ ⌘ to ask Lazur to explain a complex formula or point at the right button to format your data. You can also use dictation by holding the fn key to enter data quickly without switching back and forth between your mouse and keyboard.

faq.question: Can Lazur extract data from a PDF for me?
faq.answer: Lazur does not click buttons or edit files for you. It can guide you through the process, point out where to find tools in your apps, or help you dictate the data into your spreadsheet.

faq.question: Is it safe to use AI for financial data?
faq.answer: You should only use tools that meet your firm's security standards. Lazur processes your screen and audio only while you hold the shortcut, and it does not store your content.

faq.question: What is the best way to handle large PDF reports?
faq.answer: Break them into smaller segments or use a dedicated tool like Tabula to extract specific tables before bringing them into Excel or Google Sheets.
